title: Uniboost has no hookTypeId guard: an unwired/wrong dispatch hook silently accrues zero phUSD debt (M-04 fail-open class reborn on a third dispatcher)
description: Uniboost routes dispatched prime through a configurable mint-debt hook, but the base ATokenDispatcherV2._dispatch calls hook.onDispatch unconditionally with no hookTypeId() marker check (unlike the M-04-FIXED NudgeRatchet). The constructor defaults hook = new DefaultDispatchHook() whose onDispatch is an empty no-op (src/hooks/DefaultDispatchHook.sol:12). If the owner opens dispatches without calling setHook(uniboostMintDebtHook), or wires a mismatched hook, every Uniboost dispatch forwards prime with ZERO phUSD mint-debt accrued, with no revert and no event. This is the third dispatcher to copy the M-04-vulnerable unconditional-hook pattern and the one most analogous to the M-04-fixed NudgeRatchet.
impact: Backing-integrity feature failure (no theft, no removal of held assets): phUSD that should have been backed by accrued debt is never accrued during the unwired window. Recoverable -- setHook can be corrected at any time -- but debt that should have accrued during the window is lost-not-accrued (no retroactive backfill); the prime itself is retained on-chain.
attackPath: 1. Owner deploys Uniboost; base ATokenDispatcherV2 ctor sets hook = new DefaultDispatchHook() (no-op).
2. Owner opens dispatches WITHOUT calling setHook(uniboostMintDebtHook) (or sets the wrong hook).
3. ATokenDispatcherV2._dispatch calls hook.onDispatch unconditionally (no hookTypeId marker check, unlike the M-04-fixed NudgeRatchet) -> no debt accrues, no revert, no event.
4. Backing accounting for Uniboost-routed prime is silently zero until the owner notices and fixes the wiring.
recommendation: Apply the same hookTypeId() marker guard used by the M-04-fixed NudgeRatchet to the Uniboost dispatch path (assert hook.hookTypeId() == EXPECTED, fail-closed on the default/unwired hook). Operationally: always setHook before opening dispatches and verify debt accrual on the first dispatch.

classification.plausibility: n/a (owner-config dependent, not an attacker scenario)
classification.likelihood: low-to-moderate operational; requires an owner setup omission. No external/permissionless trigger.
classification.externalRequirements: None beyond the owner config omission; no attacker, no market condition.
classification.recoverable: Yes. setHook can be corrected at any time; only debt that should have accrued during the unwired window is lost-not-accrued (no retroactive backfill).

disposition.note: Same fail-open class as owner-accepted wont-fix Q-08 (96c60b72, BalancerPoolerV2), but on a distinct contract/function => distinct fingerprint => NOT auto-suppressed. Routed for explicit owner decision. DO NOT pre-set wont-fix -- left OPEN and proposed.
disposition.precedent: Q-08 (96c60b72) -- same fail-open class on BalancerPoolerV2, owner wont-fix.
